items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I remember playing a fundraiser for Billy Higgins – he was sick – right over here at the union, right down the street.

ctx.x: The Revolution Will Not Be Televised.

Yeah, that was it. I remember doing that. I kind of remember where it was. I think it was RCA studios up there off of Fifth Avenue, Sixth Avenue, somewhere in there. Because I used to walk around, use my bicycle to get to the studios. I put my flute on the handlebars and I’d go all different places, from one to the other, because many times I’d have more than one session during the day during those days, because there was a lot of t.v. commercials that I was doing. That’s something that’s not documented. I used…

That’s what – I think Melvin Sparks is involved in that too. We’ll come back to that. But let’s return to this issue of – this is a jazz discography. Yet your recording career spans, as you say, commercial and other genres. What about recording with symphony or orchestras? Did – do you have . . . ?
